item: A backup restore carries an article's places and entities on their own stamp, each half on its own evidence, and 'owes the re-index nothing' means both stamps (R415)
summary: The re-index PR gave the places and entities their own table, article_www_stamps; this change makes the restore use it. An article's keyword rows ride the keyword stamp and its places and entities ride the www stamp, verified separately (the www digest is the re-index PR's own function, called on the incoming row), so a title edit costs the keywords a pass and keeps the places, and a backup without the stamp carries the keywords alone. The backlog read, the stand-in lost count, the post-swap re-index skip set and the batch status all read BOTH stamps; the rowid-reuse delete covers both tables. The candidate walk reads each stamp table once by its own cursor (a first version merged them in one ordered, limited statement and rescanned the shorter table on every page: 18 s at a million articles). New report keys www_engine, www_stamped, www_verified, www_planned, www_reason, candidates, refused.www_inputs_changed, refused.article_missing, carried.keyword_articles and carried.www_articles (carried.articles now means carried completely). About 22 new tests; 41 mutants, 40 killed, the survivor equivalent. The re-index status read costs about 20 to 30 ms more at a million pending articles. Not seen in the field: driven by tests.
